city.name: Fushimi Inari
city.description: Fushimi Inari Taisha from open data: the Romon gate, the main shrine and the Senbon Torii climbing Mount Inari past Yotsutsuji, with measured heights from Project PLATEAU on GSI laser terrain.

tour.title: Fushimi Inari from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings from OpenStreetMap, Overture Maps and Project PLATEAU, on GSI 5 m laser terrain under GSI aerial photographs, and thousands of torii on the paths up Inari-yama, 233 m.

tour.title: The Romon
tour.text: Toyotomi Hideyoshi's gate of 1589, about 14 m, vermilion under hinoki bark, with the foxes of Inari before it: one holds a jewel, the other a key.

tour.title: Senbon Torii
tour.text: Two tunnels of torii side by side, counted on the ground at 382 and 399, each given by a person or a company whose name is on the back.

protection.title: No statutory sun rule for public places
protection.summary: Kyoto protects its skyline with height limits (a cap of 31 m in the busiest districts) and Japan limits shadows on homes with the Building Standards Act, but neither protects sun on parks. Sun on these places is measured for information, not tested against a rule.
protection.source_note: No legal window is transcribed for these places, so each is shown for 10:00-14:00 and none is marked protected.
protection.reading_note: Heights come from Project PLATEAU, measured from aerial survey in 2020-2021, so buildings finished since are missing or low.
protection.tip: Tip: the hillside puts the lanes in shade early on winter afternoons.

shore.encoding: r: 128 + 2 x signed distance to the shoreline (m, water positive); g: sand; b: rock

trees.note: Species are not mapped; the mix is a guess from Kyoto's street-tree surveys and the shrine's own guide. Mount Inari is a sacred wood of cedars and cypresses (sugi, standing for hinoki too) and evergreen oaks, the torii tunnels running under them; the streets below have zelkovas, ginkgos, camphors and cherries. The shrine's precinct takes a mix of its own, its outline OpenStreetMap's (pipeline/tree_areas.py).

water_bridges.note: the Keihan main line's girder bridge

sources.places: Overture base land use (OpenStreetMap, ODbL); rules: No statutory sun rule for public places
sources.trees: Overture base land, tree points and rows (OpenStreetMap, ODbL); heights not mapped

woods.encoding: r: ground cover under the canopy (0-255), g: canopy height x 8 (m), b: a footway under the canopy, a: in a wood or park
